title: Run the relocation rebind from the main checkout, not the worktree
action: A live acceptance run found the shipped relocation rebind refused every time. The belt calls `bee cells rebind-session` with a worktree cwd, and that verb is refused inside a granted feature worktree (reproduced: from the worktree it exits 1 with 'refused inside a granted feature worktree — ... FIX: run it from <main>'; from the main checkout the same call exits 0). Fix all three call sites in .pi/extensions/bee-guard.ts to pass the already-resolved `mainRoot` (computed at :1605) instead of a worktree path: the forward rebind at :1635 passes `intent.targetCwd`, and the two compensating rollbacks at :1688 and :1730 pass `intent.sourceCwd`, which is the worktree on the exit-before-merge direction. RED FIRST: the existing contract case missed this because the harness fakes the bee CLI and its stub records only argv and stdin, never the working directory — extend the stub prelude to append its own $PWD beside the argv it logs, add an assertion that the rebind invocation ran with the main checkout root, watch it fail against the current belt, then fix. Finally run `bee dev regen` so the embedded belt bytes and the release manifest match.
verify: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --test pi_plugin_contracts && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check && .bee/bin/bee doctor --runtime pi --json

truths: every bee cells rebind-session call the belt makes runs with the main checkout root as its cwd
the stub bee records the working directory of each invocation
the contract test asserts that cwd and fails against the pre-fix belt
the compensating rollback on a cancelled or failed switch also runs from the main root
doctor --runtime pi reports wiring_matches_binary ok after regen

artifacts.substantive: all three rebind call sites pass mainRoot
the stub logs its cwd and the case asserts the rebind ran from the main root

key_links: mainRoot is already computed at bee-guard.ts:1605 and is in scope for all three sites
prohibitions: Do not change the carry mechanism itself
Do not touch Claude, Codex or OpenCode paths

Forced a rebuild by touching doctor.rs and re-vendored the newer artifact — why: the first vendored binary predated the belt fix, so doctor reported wiring_matches_binary not_ok — something else had to be fixed first

checks.evidence: bee-guard.ts:1640 (forward rebind), :1693 and :1735 (compensating rollbacks) all pass `mainRoot`, the value resolved at :1605; a grep for execBeeCli call sites shows no rebind invocation carrying intent.targetCwd or intent.sourceCwd.

Against the pre-fix belt the case failed on the rebound-claim assertion — left Some("sess-old-reloc"), right Some("sess-new-reloc") — and passed after the three call sites changed: `relocation_with_a_job_in_flight_carries_inbox_and_rebinds_claims ... ok`.

The fixture's stub bee now answers `cells rebind-session` itself, refusing with the real verb's message when its cwd is the worktree and rewriting the claim (session plus fence_epoch) otherwise; before this it delegated cells verbs to the real binary, which refused, so the assertion rested on a call that rewrote nothing.

The stub logs `<cwd>\t<argv>` to its own calls_cwd.log — separate from calls.log, whose whole-line equality other cases depend on — and the case asserts every `cells rebind-session` invocation ran with the main checkout root.

Leader re-ran the approved chain in the worktree: 68 contract tests passed 0 failed; `dev release-manifest --check` reported 376 files match; `doctor --runtime pi` returned overall ready with wiring_matches_binary ok after the binary was rebuilt and re-vendored.

Commit c65eaaef13c4496b15b44d99b0ad0b8fe9e29dca touches only the belt and the Pi contract test; the regen commit 18585cf13b498f2f4847611802403171f8fe624d touches the manifest and onboarding record. The carry mechanism itself is unchanged, and no Claude, Codex or OpenCode path was edited.
